434|**Semantics settled in D4.** Pinned by the D4 tests or decided in the implementation and accepted in review.
435|
436|1. **Replay loop.** One `SimClock` is shared by World and Evaluator; faults go through `world.schedule` with `at`/`clearAt` offsets from t0. At each tick instant, as built: `scheduler.tick()`, `world.step_until(t)`, ingest every new sink entry in write order, `evaluator.tick()`. A canary planted at a tick can be fetched by a run at the same instant.
437|2. **Deployments.** Scenario `deployments` are environment names; deployment IDs are `<service>/<environment>`. A scorecard runs a contract against its own service's scenarios only, held-out ones included.
438|3. **Matching and latency.** Actual events match expected ones on (deployment, tripwire). Trip latency counts from the latest fault `at` on that environment at or before the event; recovery latency from the latest `clearAt` (the fault `at` when there is none). An event after `withinSeconds`, or before the fault, is missing and also unexpected.
439|4. **False positives** are strict: every unmatched actual trip or recovery is `unexpected`. `expected_hit_rate` = matched expected trips and recoveries / all of them (1.0 when there are none). `mustNotTrip` entries are asserted but are not expected items.
440|5. **Routing.** Entries route to a deployment by the component's `container_name` and `match` labels, then `deploymentBy`; a connector label maps through `Deployment.resources`, with `jsonPayload.environment` as the fallback.
441|6. **Arming.** `${param}` is resolved when a deployment is armed. Cadence and canary are evaluated in `tick()`, schema and errorSignature in `ingest()`. Every `TripEvent.at` is `clock.now()`. The evaluator keeps only the runs a window needs.
442|7. **Cadence** uses the latest heartbeat timestamp seen, never the last entry to arrive.
443|8. **Isolation** (T8) compares (kind, deployment, tripwire) only, never `runId` or `insertId`, which are global counters.
444|9. **Canary scheduler** plants through `World.plant_canary`, first at arm + `everyMinutes`, then every `everyMinutes`, only for deployments whose contract has a synthetic tripwire.
445|10. **Change point.** Overrides take the contract's `changePoint.overrides` shape; cadence re-arms at entry; overrides revert after `duration_s`. The executor calls `enter_change_point(deployment, component, duration_s=..., overrides=contract.changePoint.overrides)` after an approved change (D6).
446|11. **Cost.** The scenario-library tests share module-scoped scorecards.
447|12. **Known weakness.** With errorSignature recovery after `windowRuns − threshold + 1` clean runs, `flap-severe` (rate 0.7) passes on its seed partly by luck: about 2 seeds in 3 would see a 3-clean streak and a recovery. A symmetric rule (recover when at least `threshold` of the last `windowRuns` runs are clean) is more robust; deferred until after the hackathon.

436|1. **Replay loop.** One `SimClock` is shared by World and Evaluator; faults go through `world.schedule` with `at`/`clearAt` offsets from t0. At each tick instant, as built: `scheduler.tick()`, `world.step_until(t)`, ingest every new sink entry in write order, `evaluator.tick()`. A canary planted at a tick can be fetched by a run at the same instant.
437|2. **Deployments.** Scenario `deployments` are environment names; deployment IDs are `<service>/<environment>`. A scorecard runs a contract against its own service's scenarios only, held-out ones included.
438|3. **Matching and latency.** Actual events match expected ones on (deployment, tripwire). Trip latency counts from the latest fault `at` on that environment at or before the event; recovery latency from the latest `clearAt` (the fault `at` when there is none). An event after `withinSeconds`, or before the fault, is missing and also unexpected.
439|4. **False positives** are strict: every unmatched actual trip or recovery is `unexpected`. `expected_hit_rate` = matched expected trips and recoveries / all of them (1.0 when there are none). `mustNotTrip` entries are asserted but are not expected items.
440|5. **Routing.** Entries route to a deployment by the component's `container_name` and `match` labels, then `deploymentBy`; a connector label maps through `Deployment.resources`, with `jsonPayload.environment` as the fallback.
441|6. **Arming.** `${param}` is resolved when a deployment is armed. Cadence and canary are evaluated in `tick()`, schema and errorSignature in `ingest()`. Every `TripEvent.at` is `clock.now()`. The evaluator keeps only the runs a window needs.
442|7. **Cadence** uses the latest heartbeat timestamp seen, never the last entry to arrive.
443|8. **Isolation** (T8) compares (kind, deployment, tripwire) only, never `runId` or `insertId`, which are global counters.
444|9. **Canary scheduler** plants through `World.plant_canary`, first at arm + `everyMinutes`, then every `everyMinutes`, only for deployments whose contract has a synthetic tripwire.
445|10. **Change point.** Overrides take the contract's `changePoint.overrides` shape; cadence re-arms at entry; overrides revert after `duration_s`. The executor calls `enter_change_point(deployment, component, duration_s=..., overrides=contract.changePoint.overrides)` after an approved change (D6).
446|11. **Cost.** The scenario-library tests share module-scoped scorecards.
447|12. **Known weakness.** With errorSignature recovery after `windowRuns − threshold + 1` clean runs, `flap-severe` (rate 0.7) passes on its seed partly by luck: about 2 seeds in 3 would see a 3-clean streak and a recovery. A symmetric rule (recover when at least `threshold` of the last `windowRuns` runs are clean) is more robust; deferred until after the hackathon.

22|
23|## 1. Summary
24|
25|Fleet SRE is an agentic site reliability engineer for MSSPs running multi-tenant Google SecOps SOAR. It writes each service's monitoring contract, investigates when a tripwire fires and proposes a fix for a human to approve. The platform underneath exists only to give it safe tools and deterministic checks.
26|
27|- **Problem.** An MSSP runs many tenants (SOAR environments) across many services in one instance. Connectors fail silently, a `LIVE` status can sit on a connector that ingests nothing, and each tenant's monitoring depends on who onboarded it.
28|- **What the SRE does.** Authors one contract per service version, investigates incidents with read-only tools and proposes allowlisted actions. The platform writes the postmortem from the incident record. Drafting contract amendments is designed but cut (§9).
29|- **Why it can be trusted.** It isn't. Deterministic code grades every output: contracts by a chaos scorecard, evidence when it is recorded, diagnoses when they are submitted, fixes by tripwires.
30|- **Fleet leverage.** Amendments land on the service contract, so one tenant's incident hardens every tenant on that service. (Designed; the amendment step is cut, §9.)
31|- **Built on.** A local-first Python system with a mock SecOps built against Google's published Chronicle API and SOAR log format, with Cloud Logging and IAM on a personal GCP project (Pub/Sub, Cloud Run and Firestore are cut, §9).
32|- **Entry.** Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, Indie track, "Build for Your World" theme. Submission due 2026-11-04 at 9:00 PM ET.
33|
34|## 2. Design principles
35|
36|1. **Verified, not trusted.** Every SRE output has a deterministic check: a contract must pass the chaos scorecard, evidence must exist when it is recorded, a diagnosis must rest on recorded evidence of the right kind, a fix must pass change-point tripwires.
37|2. **Reason once, run cheap.** The model works when a contract is written or amended and when an incident opens. No model sits in the watch loop.
38|3. **One contract per service.** The contract versions with the service definition. Per-tenant differences are parameters. The platform uses whatever integration version is installed; upgrades are a separate process.
39|4. **Every incident hardens every tenant.** Amendments land on the service contract, so a gap found on one tenant closes for all of them.
40|5. **The agent holds no credentials.** Read tools are proxied by the platform under a read-only identity; writes need human approval and run under a separate identity. IAM enforces this and tests prove it.
41|6. **Built against Google's spec.** Mock resources and log labels copy the published Chronicle API and SOAR logging docs, so the mock can be swapped for a real instance. What is invented is labelled as invented (see `mocks.md` §9).
42|7. **Local first.** Everything runs on a laptop with `make demo`. GCP services are adapters behind ports, swapped in late.
43|8. **The same rule applies to the build.** Humans write what defines correctness (contracts, scenarios, expected outcomes, acceptance test specs, SRE prompts in `prompts/`). The coding agent writes what is graded against them.
44|9. **Checks live inside the tools.** A gate runs inside the tool that moves work forward (recording evidence, submitting a diagnosis), never as a separate tool the model may choose to call, because a confident model skips optional checks. A refused call comes back as an error the model reads and fixes. The model chooses every call; code never hard-codes the order.
45|
46|Field lessons that shape the tripwires: absence-only detection cannot tell quiet from broken, and a field changing type (severity arriving as a string) passes every volume check.
47|
48|## 3. The SRE loop
49|
50|The model acts at two points (author, investigate); closing is deterministic (step 7). Deterministic code grades each output before anything changes; inside an investigation, the gates sit in the tools (§6.1).
51|
52|```mermaid
53|flowchart LR
54|  A["Write contract (SRE)"] --> B["Chaos scorecard"] --> C{"Passes?"}
55|  C -- "no: revise" --> A
56|  C -- "yes" --> D["Approve contract (human)"] --> E["Tripwires watch"]
57|  E -- "tripwire fires" --> F["Investigate (SRE)"]
58|  F -- "escalates or hits a limit" --> N["Needs input (human)"]
59|  N -- "reply, more turns, or fault state changed" --> F
60|  F -- "proposes action" --> G["Approve fix (human)"]
61|  G -- "rejected with notes" --> F
62|  G -- "approved" --> H["Apply fix (deployer identity)"] --> I{"Verified?"}
63|  F -- "no action: verify recovery" --> I
64|  I -- "no: retry, max 2, then escalate" --> F
65|  I -- "yes" --> J["Close incident (postmortem)"]
66|  J -. "gap found: amend (cut)" .-> A
67|```
68|
69|1. **Author.** Given a service brief, sample logs and parameters, the SRE drafts a contract. The harness scores it; the SRE revises against the scorecard (max 3 revisions); a human approves.
70|2. **Watch.** The evaluator runs every deployment's tripwires. No model call.
71|3. **Investigate.** A trip opens an incident. The SRE states hypotheses, investigates with read tools, records evidence that is checked as it is recorded, and submits a diagnosis through a gated tool (§6.1). The diagnosis proposes one action, proposes no action and asks for verification, or escalates.
72|4. **Hand off.** An escalation, or an investigation that hits a limit, pauses the incident at NEEDS_INPUT. No model calls are made while it waits. It resumes the same session only when something changed: a human replied, more turns were granted, or the incident's tripwire state changed (for example, a credential was rotated outside the platform).
73|5. **Approve and apply.** A human sees hypotheses, evidence and the patch diff, and approves or rejects with notes; notes go back to the SRE as its next message. On approval the executor journals its intent, then applies the change under the deployer identity.
74|6. **Verify.** A change-point window tightens checks on that component. The diagnosis states the expected outcome; the tripwires decide. Failure returns to investigation at most twice, then escalates.
75|7. **Close and learn.** The platform writes the postmortem from the incident record: timeline, pauses and what resumed them, category, action and transcripts. Amendment (the SRE drafts a contract change after a late or missing trip; it is rescored, approved and applied to every deployment of the service) is designed but cut (§9).

116|## 5. Contracts and tripwires
117|
118|A contract is one JSON file per service version. Deployments supply parameters only. Full schema: `contracts/schema.json` (D1).
119|
120|```json
121|{
122|  "service": "alert-ingestion",
123|  "version": "1.0.0",
124|  "parameters": {
125|    "expectedAlertsPerHour": { "type": "number", "required": true },
126|    "intervalSeconds": { "type": "integer", "required": true }
127|  },
128|  "components": [
129|    { "id": "connector", "kind": "connectorInstance",
130|      "logs": { "container_name": "python", "match": ["connector_name", "connector_instance"], "deploymentBy": "labels.connector_instance" } },
131|    { "id": "ingestion", "kind": "etlFlow",
132|      "logs": { "container_name": "etl", "match": ["correlation_id"], "deploymentBy": "jsonPayload.environment" } }
133|  ],
134|  "tripwires": [
135|    { "id": "dead-connector", "component": "connector", "type": "cadence",
136|      "spec": { "event": "connector.run.completed", "intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}", "maxSilentIntervals": 3 } },
137|    { "id": "canary", "component": "ingestion", "type": "synthetic",
138|      "spec": { "everyMinutes": 10, "deadlineSeconds": 180 } },
139|    { "id": "priority-shape", "component": "ingestion", "type": "schema",
140|      "spec": { "event": "alert.ingested", "field": "jsonPayload.alert.priority", "type": "integer", "enum": [-1, 40, 60, 80, 100], "required": true, "consecutive": 1, "recoverAfter": 20 } },
141|    { "id": "connector-errors", "component": "connector", "type": "errorSignature",
142|      "spec": { "minSeverity": "WARNING", "windowRuns": 10, "threshold": 8 } }
143|  ],
144|  "changePoint": { "durationSeconds": 1800, "overrides": { "dead-connector": { "maxSilentIntervals": 2 } } },
145|  "provenance": { "authoredBy": "<model id>", "scorecard": "<run id>", "approvedBy": "<human>" }
146|}
147|```
148|
149|Values were settled in D1; `contracts/*.json` is authoritative and this example matches it. The `intel-sync` contract has one `jobInstance` component and three tripwires: `dead-job` (cadence on `job.run.completed`, 3 silent intervals), `hollow-run` (schema on `job.run.completed` entries whose `status` is `SUCCESS`: `jsonPayload.indicatorsSynced` ≥ 1, tripping after 3 consecutive violations and recovering after 2 valid runs) and `job-errors` (errorSignature, 2 ERROR runs in the last 3).
150|
151|**Contract rules settled in D1.**
152|
153|- `logs.deploymentBy` names the entry field that identifies the deployment: `labels.connector_instance` for connectors, and the invented `jsonPayload.environment` for jobs and ETL. Google's documented job label (`job_name`) names the job definition, which is the same on every tenant, and ETL entries carry only `correlation_id`.
154|- Cadence specs name their interval explicitly (`"intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}"`).
155|- Schema tripwires take `event` (only entries with that `jsonPayload.event` are checked), `where` (equality filters on other fields), `consecutive` (violations in a row to trip; default 1) and `recoverAfter` (valid entries in a row to recover; default `consecutive`). Entries the filters exclude neither count nor reset either run.
156|- For `errorSignature`, a run is one `runId`, its severity is the worst entry in it, and it is judged when it completes (the component's cadence heartbeat). It trips when at least `threshold` of the last `windowRuns` runs are at or above `minSeverity`, and recovers after `windowRuns − threshold + 1` clean runs in a row.
157|- Entering a change point re-arms cadence from that moment: a heartbeat from before the change point never counts.
158|- Cadence goes by the latest heartbeat timestamp seen, not the last entry to arrive, and trips when the silence is strictly longer than `maxSilentIntervals × intervalSeconds`. It recovers on the first heartbeat that clears that condition.
159|- A canary seen exactly at its deadline is in time. A late canary does not recover the tripwire; the next canary seen in time does.
160|- `load_contract` rejects a bad contract with a `ContractError` code (table in `deliverables.md` §D1).
161|
162|| Tripwire type | Checks | Trips when | Failure it catches |
163|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
164|| `cadence` | A named heartbeat event (connector run, job run) against the deployment's interval | No event for N intervals | A stopped connector or job. Runs happen on schedule regardless of alert volume, so quiet tenants do not false-alarm |
165|| `synthetic` | A planted canary alert traced end to end by `correlation_id` | The canary misses its deadline | End-to-end breakage with a healthy-looking status |
166|| `schema` | Field presence, type and allowed values on ingested events | A required field is missing, the wrong type, or out of range | Silent type breakage that volume checks miss |
167|| `errorSignature` | WARNING/ERROR rate in a component's logs over the last N runs | Count ≥ threshold | A per-tenant credential Green Liar, without planting anything in the client's SIEM |
168|
169|**Canary scope.** In the demo the canary is planted in the fake upstream per tenant. In production, planting into a client's workspace is off the table, so the canary runs on one MSSP-owned canary tenant per service version (proves the code path), and `errorSignature` covers per-tenant credential failures.

171|### 5.1 Chaos harness and scorecard
172|
173|- **Scenario library** (`fixtures/scenarios/<service>/*.yaml`, human-authored): fleet, duration, fault schedule, expected trips with a maximum detection latency, and `mustNotTrip`.
174|- **Replay**: the mock world generates each scenario's log stream on a `SimClock`; the stream runs through the evaluator. No GCP, seconds per run.
175|- **Scorecard**: per scenario, expected versus actual trips, detection latency, false positives. A contract passes only at 100% expected trips and zero false positives.
176|- **The SRE never writes scenarios or expected outcomes.** It sees scorecard results only.
177|- **Held-out scenarios.** Some scenarios are marked `holdout: true`. They never appear in revision feedback, not even by ID. A contract passes only if the holdouts pass too; when only a holdout fails, the feedback says "a held-out scenario failed" and nothing more. This stops the authoring loop from fitting the visible scenarios.

179|## 6. The investigation: loop, tools, actions and gates
180|
181|### 6.1 The loop
182|
183|Each turn, the gateway sends the full history to the Meta Model API (Responses API, `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, encrypted reasoning included and replayed; §8). The model returns one tool call; the platform runs it; the result, or the gate's refusal, goes back as the next input. The session is saved after every turn.
184|
185|- **One tool per turn.** A reply with no tool call gets "Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool." and counts as a turn. If a response holds more than one call, only the first runs.
186|- **Last turn.** On the final turn the SRE is told to submit with what it has.
187|- **Rationale.** Every tool call carries a required `rationale` (at most 200 characters). The model's reasoning tokens are not readable (Chat Completions returns no `reasoning_content`; Responses returns it encrypted), so `rationale` is the visible "think" line in the trace and the UI timeline.
188|- **Ending.**
189|
190|| Ends with | Incident goes to | Model calls afterwards |
191|| --- | --- | --- |
192|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `propose` | AWAITING_APPROVAL | None until approval or rejection |
193|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `none` | VERIFYING | None |
194|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `escalate` | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `escalated` | None until resumed |
195|| Three refused submissions | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `refused` | None until resumed |
196|| Turn limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `budget` | None until resumed |
197|| Token limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `token_budget` | None until resumed |
198|| The same read call a third time in a segment | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `stuck` | None until resumed |
199|| Model API still failing after retries | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `model_unavailable` | None until resumed |
200|
201|- **Resume.** A NEEDS_INPUT incident resumes the same session (hypotheses and evidence kept) only when a human replied, granted more turns, or the incident's tripwire state changed since it paused. Otherwise resume is refused without a model call. What changed is the SRE's next message.
202|- **Gates off (evals only).** Gates can be switched off to measure what they catch; each verdict they would have given is still recorded. The incident manager and the web app refuse an investigator with gates off.
203|
204|### 6.2 Read tools (proxied, read-only identity)
205|
206|Every read tool also takes `rationale`. Reads are capped per segment: 12 in the first, 4 more after each resume. A read over the cap is refused with an error, and the loop continues. A component that is not one of the service's component IDs is refused rather than answered with empty data.
207|
208|| Tool | Returns | Backed by |
209|| --- | --- | --- |
210|| `query_logs(deployment, window, filter)` | Log entries with `insertId` | `LogQuery` port |
211|| `get_resource(name)` | A connector instance, job instance, integration instance or environment | Mock Chronicle API `get` |
212|| `list_connector_logs(connectorInstance)` | Recent `ConnectorLog` records (empty unless log collection is on for that instance) | Mock `connectorInstances.logs.list` |
213|| `list_job_logs(jobInstance)` | Recent `JobInstanceLog` records | Mock `jobInstances.logs.list` |
214|| `test_integration_instance(name)` | Connectivity test result | Mock `integrationInstances.executeTest` (changes no state) |
215|| `compare_siblings(service, component, window)` | The same component's signals across every deployment of the service | Platform, computed |
216|| `tripwire_history(deployment)` | Recent trips, recoveries and approved changes | Platform state |
217|| `get_contract(service)` | Current contract and its last scorecard | Platform registry |

219|### 6.3 Working tools and their gates
220|
221|The gates run inside these tools. A refused call returns `{"error": "...", "problems": ["..."]}` and never raises. Each problem starts with the rule it broke (`evidence.value: …`); the rule codes are listed in `docs/d5-pins.md`. Every tool result reaches the model as `{"callId": "...", "result": {...}}`, because the model cannot read call IDs back from the replayed history (D2 finding). A tool source's `field` is a dotted path into `result` (`successful`, not `result.successful`).
222|
223|| Tool | Does | Gate (inside the tool) |
224|| --- | --- | --- |
225|| `set_hypotheses(items)` | Sets 2–4 hypotheses, each with a statement and the evidence that would confirm it | 2–4 items; at least one marked `alternative: true` (a competing explanation, such as "this is fleet-wide, not specific to this tenant"). Required before `record_evidence` or `submit_diagnosis`. Calling it again replaces the set; evidence for removed hypotheses is dropped |
226|| `update_plan(plan)` | Records how the SRE will settle each hypothesis | None |
227|| `record_evidence(hypothesis, stance, source, why)` | Records one piece of evidence for (`supports`) or against (`refutes`) one hypothesis. `source` is `{insertId}` for a log entry or `{callId, field, value}` for a tool result | Log source: the `insertId` exists and belongs to the incident's deployment or to a sibling deployment the SRE queried in this session. Tool source: `callId` is a call made in this session and its result has `field` equal to `value`. The hypothesis exists. At most 3 items per hypothesis. Returns the evidence ID (`E1`, `E2`, …) and the hypotheses that still have no evidence |
228|| `submit_diagnosis(diagnosis)` | Submits the diagnosis (§6.5) | The submission rules in §6.5 |

245|### 6.5 Diagnosis schema and submission rules
246|
247|```json
248|{
249|  "incidentId": "string",
250|  "deployment": "string",
251|  "component": "string",
252|  "category": "connector_stalled | job_stalled | credential_failure | schema_drift | job_hollow_success | job_failing | unknown",
253|  "hypothesis": "ID of the hypothesis the SRE concludes (from set_hypotheses)",
254|  "summary": "the conclusion in one or two sentences",
255|  "evidence": ["E1", "E3"],
256|  "openQuestions": [ { "hypothesis": "string", "why": "string" } ],
257|  "action": {
258|    "type": "propose | none | escalate",
259|    "method": "one of the allowlist, when type is propose",
260|    "resource": "full resource name",
261|    "updateMask": ["field"],
262|    "patch": {},
263|    "escalationSummary": "string, when type is escalate"
264|  },
265|  "expectedVerification": { "tripwire": "string", "condition": "recovers_within", "seconds": 0 },
266|  "rollback": "string",
267|  "confidence": "low | medium | high"
268|}
269|```
270|
271|`category` is an enum so evaluations grade deterministically. The tool schema sets `additionalProperties: false` throughout.
272|
273|`submit_diagnosis` refuses a diagnosis, listing every problem, unless:
274|
275|1. **Schema.** It validates against the schema above.
276|2. **Recorded evidence only.** Every ID in `evidence` was recorded in this session.
277|3. **Hypothesis coverage.** The concluded hypothesis has at least one cited `supports` item. Every other hypothesis has at least one recorded `refutes` item or an entry in `openQuestions`.
278|4. **Category evidence rule.** The cited evidence includes what the category requires (table below).
279|5. **Action.** `propose`: the method is in §6.4, `updateMask` is within its allowed fields, the patch keys are within `updateMask`, and `resource` is the deployment's own connector instance (`connectorInstances.*`) or job instance (`jobInstances.*`). `propose` and `none`: `expectedVerification.tripwire` is a tripwire of the incident's deployment. `none`: at least one cited item was recorded after the session's most recent resume. `escalate`: `escalationSummary` is not empty.
280|
281|After three refused submissions the incident goes to NEEDS_INPUT with reason `refused`.
282|
283|**Category evidence rules.** These check deterministically that the evidence is the right kind for the conclusion. They stand in for the model-judged "claims check" other agents use.
284|
285|| Category | Cited evidence must include |
286|| --- | --- |
287|| `connector_stalled` | The deployment's latest `connector.run.completed` entry at or before the trip (that exact entry) |
288|| `job_stalled` | The deployment's latest `job.run.completed` entry at or before the trip (that exact entry) |
289|| `credential_failure` | A WARNING or ERROR entry from the deployment's connector, and a `test_integration_instance` result for the deployment's own integration instance with `successful: false` |
290|| `schema_drift` | An entry of the deployment that violates one of its schema tripwires |
291|| `job_hollow_success` | A `job.run.completed` entry of the deployment with `status: SUCCESS` and `indicatorsSynced: 0` |
292|| `job_failing` | A `job.run.error` entry, or a `job.run.completed` entry with `status: ERROR` |
293|| `unknown` | Nothing, but the action must be `escalate` |

295|### 6.6 Guardrails
296|
297|- **Gates inside the tools** (§6.3, §6.5). Refusals are fed back to the model; nothing is retried silently.
298|- **Budgets.** Per segment of an investigation (the first run, then each resume): 24 turns, 12 read calls and 400,000 tokens (input plus output) at first, then `extra_turns` and 4 read calls per resume; all configurable. Two remediation attempts per incident.
299|- **Stuck detection.** The same read tool with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time in a segment pauses the session with reason `stuck` before the call runs. Working tools are exempt: repeating one changes state, and repeated refused submissions reach the refusal cap.
300|- **Concurrency.** The executor rejects a patch if the resource changed since the SRE read it.
301|- **Executor journal.** Append-only. Before any write the executor appends `intent` (approval ID, proposal hash, the resource version read at proposal time), then `started`, then `terminal` with the result. No write happens without a durable `intent` first. On restart, an `intent` without `terminal` is reconciled by re-reading the resource: if the change is already there it is marked done; otherwise it is applied once.
302|- **Recorded replay.** Live investigations chosen as fixtures (`fixtures/recorded/`) replay offline in CI through the scripted transport. Any difference in tool calls, gate verdicts or the final diagnosis blocks the merge.
303|- **Model calls.** Exponential backoff (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 s) on 429 and 5xx; a 120 s request timeout counts as a 5xx; diagnoses cached on the public instance; spend caps.
304|- **Import boundary.** `fleetsre.sre` may not import GCP clients or the Chronicle client directly; it reaches the world only through the tool set.

21|---
22|
23|## 1. Summary
24|
25|Fleet SRE is an agentic site reliability engineer for MSSPs running multi-tenant Google SecOps SOAR. It writes each service's monitoring contract, investigates when a tripwire fires and proposes a fix for a human to approve. The platform underneath exists only to give it safe tools and deterministic checks.
26|
27|- **Problem.** An MSSP runs many tenants (SOAR environments) across many services in one instance. Connectors fail silently, a `LIVE` status can sit on a connector that ingests nothing, and each tenant's monitoring depends on who onboarded it.
28|- **What the SRE does.** Authors one contract per service version, investigates incidents with read-only tools and proposes allowlisted actions. The platform writes the postmortem from the incident record. Drafting contract amendments is designed but cut (§9).
29|- **Why it can be trusted.** It isn't. Deterministic code grades every output: contracts by a chaos scorecard, evidence when it is recorded, diagnoses when they are submitted, fixes by tripwires.
30|- **Fleet leverage.** Amendments land on the service contract, so one tenant's incident hardens every tenant on that service. (Designed; the amendment step is cut, §9.)
31|- **Built on.** A local-first Python system with a mock SecOps built against Google's published Chronicle API and SOAR log format, with Cloud Logging and IAM on a personal GCP project (Pub/Sub, Cloud Run and Firestore are cut, §9).
32|- **Entry.** Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, Indie track, "Build for Your World" theme. Submission due 2026-11-04 at 9:00 PM ET.
33|
34|## 2. Design principles
35|
36|1. **Verified, not trusted.** Every SRE output has a deterministic check: a contract must pass the chaos scorecard, evidence must exist when it is recorded, a diagnosis must rest on recorded evidence of the right kind, a fix must pass change-point tripwires.
37|2. **Reason once, run cheap.** The model works when a contract is written or amended and when an incident opens. No model sits in the watch loop.
38|3. **One contract per service.** The contract versions with the service definition. Per-tenant differences are parameters. The platform uses whatever integration version is installed; upgrades are a separate process.
39|4. **Every incident hardens every tenant.** Amendments land on the service contract, so a gap found on one tenant closes for all of them.
40|5. **The agent holds no credentials.** Read tools are proxied by the platform under a read-only identity; writes need human approval and run under a separate identity. IAM enforces this and tests prove it.
41|6. **Built against Google's spec.** Mock resources and log labels copy the published Chronicle API and SOAR logging docs, so the mock can be swapped for a real instance. What is invented is labelled as invented (see `mocks.md` §9).
42|7. **Local first.** Everything runs on a laptop with `make demo`. GCP services are adapters behind ports, swapped in late.
43|8. **The same rule applies to the build.** Humans write what defines correctness (contracts, scenarios, expected outcomes, acceptance test specs, SRE prompts in `prompts/`). The coding agent writes what is graded against them.
44|9. **Checks live inside the tools.** A gate runs inside the tool that moves work forward (recording evidence, submitting a diagnosis), never as a separate tool the model may choose to call, because a confident model skips optional checks. A refused call comes back as an error the model reads and fixes. The model chooses every call; code never hard-codes the order.
45|
46|Field lessons that shape the tripwires: absence-only detection cannot tell quiet from broken, and a field changing type (severity arriving as a string) passes every volume check.
47|
48|## 3. The SRE loop
49|
50|The model acts at two points (author, investigate); closing is deterministic (step 7). Deterministic code grades each output before anything changes; inside an investigation, the gates sit in the tools (§6.1).
51|
52|```mermaid
53|flowchart LR
54|  A["Write contract (SRE)"] --> B["Chaos scorecard"] --> C{"Passes?"}
55|  C -- "no: revise" --> A
56|  C -- "yes" --> D["Approve contract (human)"] --> E["Tripwires watch"]
57|  E -- "tripwire fires" --> F["Investigate (SRE)"]
58|  F -- "escalates or hits a limit" --> N["Needs input (human)"]
59|  N -- "reply, more turns, or fault state changed" --> F
60|  F -- "proposes action" --> G["Approve fix (human)"]
61|  G -- "rejected with notes" --> F
62|  G -- "approved" --> H["Apply fix (deployer identity)"] --> I{"Verified?"}
63|  F -- "no action: verify recovery" --> I
64|  I -- "no: retry, max 2, then escalate" --> F
65|  I -- "yes" --> J["Close incident (postmortem)"]
66|  J -. "gap found: amend (cut)" .-> A
67|```
68|
69|1. **Author.** Given a service brief, sample logs and parameters, the SRE drafts a contract. The harness scores it; the SRE revises against the scorecard (max 3 revisions); a human approves.
70|2. **Watch.** The evaluator runs every deployment's tripwires. No model call.
71|3. **Investigate.** A trip opens an incident. The SRE states hypotheses, investigates with read tools, records evidence that is checked as it is recorded, and submits a diagnosis through a gated tool (§6.1). The diagnosis proposes one action, proposes no action and asks for verification, or escalates.
72|4. **Hand off.** An escalation, or an investigation that hits a limit, pauses the incident at NEEDS_INPUT. No model calls are made while it waits. It resumes the same session only when something changed: a human replied, more turns were granted, or the incident's tripwire state changed (for example, a credential was rotated outside the platform).
73|5. **Approve and apply.** A human sees hypotheses, evidence and the patch diff, and approves or rejects with notes; notes go back to the SRE as its next message. On approval the executor journals its intent, then applies the change under the deployer identity.
74|6. **Verify.** A change-point window tightens checks on that component. The diagnosis states the expected outcome; the tripwires decide. Failure returns to investigation at most twice, then escalates.
75|7. **Close and learn.** The platform writes the postmortem from the incident record: timeline, pauses and what resumed them, category, action and transcripts. Amendment (the SRE drafts a contract change after a late or missing trip; it is rescored, approved and applied to every deployment of the service) is designed but cut (§9).
76|
77|## 4. The platform
78|
79|### 4.1 Domain model
80|
81|- **Service**: a versioned contract (components + tripwires). Two ship: `alert-ingestion` (connector instance + ETL flow) and `intel-sync` (job instance).
82|- **Deployment**: a service applied to one SOAR environment, with parameters. Adding a deployment arms its tripwires.
83|- **Component**: one Chronicle resource per deployment, found in logs by its labels.
84|- **Incident**: opened by a trip; holds the investigation session (hypotheses, recorded evidence, transcript), the diagnosis, approvals and rejections, executor journal records, the verification result and the postmortem.
85|
86|### 4.2 Ports and adapters
87|
88|| Port | Local adapter (D3–D6) | GCP adapter (D7) |
89|| --- | --- | --- |
90|| `LogSink` | JSONL file | Cloud Logging `entries.write` |
91|| `LogSource` | JSONL replay / tail | Pub/Sub push from a log sink |
92|| `LogQuery` (SRE `query_logs`) | Scan JSONL store | Cloud Logging `entries.list` |
93|| `StateStore` | SQLite | Firestore |
94|| `Clock` | `SimClock` (tests, harness) or wall clock | Wall clock + Cloud Scheduler tick |
95|| `ChronicleClient` | Mock API over HTTP | Same mock on Cloud Run (a real instance is out of scope) |
96|
97|The local log format is Cloud Logging's `LogEntry` JSON (see `mocks.md` §5), so fixtures, local replay and Cloud Logging share one structure.
98|
99|### 4.3 Runtime (deployed)
100|
101|Designed, not deployed: the re-plan (§9) keeps Cloud Logging and IAM only.
102|
103|```mermaid
104|flowchart LR
105|  M["Mock SecOps (Cloud Run)"] -- logs --> L["Cloud Logging"] -- sink --> P["Pub/Sub"] -- push --> EV["Evaluator"]
106|  S["Cloud Scheduler"] -- tick --> EV
107|  EV -- "opens incident" --> SRE["SRE runtime"]
108|  SRE <-- reasoning --> API["Meta Model API"]
109|  SRE -. "read tools" .-> L
110|  SRE -. "read tools" .-> M
111|  SRE -- proposal --> HA["Human approval (UI)"] -- approved --> X["Executor"] -- writes --> M
112|```
113|
114|State (deployments, tripwire state, incidents, investigation sessions, approvals, executor journal, transcripts) lives in Firestore when deployed, SQLite locally. The evaluator needs a clock as well as events, because silence never arrives as a message.
115|
116|## 5. Contracts and tripwires
117|
118|A contract is one JSON file per service version. Deployments supply parameters only. Full schema: `contracts/schema.json` (D1).
119|
120|```json
121|{
122|  "service": "alert-ingestion",
123|  "version": "1.0.0",
124|  "parameters": {
125|    "expectedAlertsPerHour": { "type": "number", "required": true },
126|    "intervalSeconds": { "type": "integer", "required": true }
127|  },
128|  "components": [
129|    { "id": "connector", "kind": "connectorInstance",
130|      "logs": { "container_name": "python", "match": ["connector_name", "connector_instance"], "deploymentBy": "labels.connector_instance" } },
131|    { "id": "ingestion", "kind": "etlFlow",
132|      "logs": { "container_name": "etl", "match": ["correlation_id"], "deploymentBy": "jsonPayload.environment" } }
133|  ],
134|  "tripwires": [
135|    { "id": "dead-connector", "component": "connector", "type": "cadence",
136|      "spec": { "event": "connector.run.completed", "intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}", "maxSilentIntervals": 3 } },
137|    { "id": "canary", "component": "ingestion", "type": "synthetic",
138|      "spec": { "everyMinutes": 10, "deadlineSeconds": 180 } },
139|    { "id": "priority-shape", "component": "ingestion", "type": "schema",
140|      "spec": { "event": "alert.ingested", "field": "jsonPayload.alert.priority", "type": "integer", "enum": [-1, 40, 60, 80, 100], "required": true, "consecutive": 1, "recoverAfter": 20 } },
141|    { "id": "connector-errors", "component": "connector", "type": "errorSignature",
142|      "spec": { "minSeverity": "WARNING", "windowRuns": 10, "threshold": 8 } }
143|  ],
144|  "changePoint": { "durationSeconds": 1800, "overrides": { "dead-connector": { "maxSilentIntervals": 2 } } },
145|  "provenance": { "authoredBy": "<model id>", "scorecard": "<run id>", "approvedBy": "<human>" }
146|}
147|```
148|
149|Values were settled in D1; `contracts/*.json` is authoritative and this example matches it. The `intel-sync` contract has one `jobInstance` component and three tripwires: `dead-job` (cadence on `job.run.completed`, 3 silent intervals), `hollow-run` (schema on `job.run.completed` entries whose `status` is `SUCCESS`: `jsonPayload.indicatorsSynced` ≥ 1, tripping after 3 consecutive violations and recovering after 2 valid runs) and `job-errors` (errorSignature, 2 ERROR runs in the last 3).
150|
151|**Contract rules settled in D1.**
152|
153|- `logs.deploymentBy` names the entry field that identifies the deployment: `labels.connector_instance` for connectors, and the invented `jsonPayload.environment` for jobs and ETL. Google's documented job label (`job_name`) names the job definition, which is the same on every tenant, and ETL entries carry only `correlation_id`.
154|- Cadence specs name their interval explicitly (`"intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}"`).
155|- Schema tripwires take `event` (only entries with that `jsonPayload.event` are checked), `where` (equality filters on other fields), `consecutive` (violations in a row to trip; default 1) and `recoverAfter` (valid entries in a row to recover; default `consecutive`). Entries the filters exclude neither count nor reset either run.
156|- For `errorSignature`, a run is one `runId`, its severity is the worst entry in it, and it is judged when it completes (the component's cadence heartbeat). It trips when at least `threshold` of the last `windowRuns` runs are at or above `minSeverity`, and recovers after `windowRuns − threshold + 1` clean runs in a row.
157|- Entering a change point re-arms cadence from that moment: a heartbeat from before the change point never counts.
158|- Cadence goes by the latest heartbeat timestamp seen, not the last entry to arrive, and trips when the silence is strictly longer than `maxSilentIntervals × intervalSeconds`. It recovers on the first heartbeat that clears that condition.
159|- A canary seen exactly at its deadline is in time. A late canary does not recover the tripwire; the next canary seen in time does.
160|- `load_contract` rejects a bad contract with a `ContractError` code (table in `deliverables.md` §D1).
161|
162|| Tripwire type | Checks | Trips when | Failure it catches |
163|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
164|| `cadence` | A named heartbeat event (connector run, job run) against the deployment's interval | No event for N intervals | A stopped connector or job. Runs happen on schedule regardless of alert volume, so quiet tenants do not false-alarm |
165|| `synthetic` | A planted canary alert traced end to end by `correlation_id` | The canary misses its deadline | End-to-end breakage with a healthy-looking status |
166|| `schema` | Field presence, type and allowed values on ingested events | A required field is missing, the wrong type, or out of range | Silent type breakage that volume checks miss |
167|| `errorSignature` | WARNING/ERROR rate in a component's logs over the last N runs | Count ≥ threshold | A per-tenant credential Green Liar, without planting anything in the client's SIEM |
168|
169|**Canary scope.** In the demo the canary is planted in the fake upstream per tenant. In production, planting into a client's workspace is off the table, so the canary runs on one MSSP-owned canary tenant per service version (proves the code path), and `errorSignature` covers per-tenant credential failures.
170|
171|### 5.1 Chaos harness and scorecard
172|
173|- **Scenario library** (`fixtures/scenarios/<service>/*.yaml`, human-authored): fleet, duration, fault schedule, expected trips with a maximum detection latency, and `mustNotTrip`.
174|- **Replay**: the mock world generates each scenario's log stream on a `SimClock`; the stream runs through the evaluator. No GCP, seconds per run.
175|- **Scorecard**: per scenario, expected versus actual trips, detection latency, false positives. A contract passes only at 100% expected trips and zero false positives.
176|- **The SRE never writes scenarios or expected outcomes.** It sees scorecard results only.
177|- **Held-out scenarios.** Some scenarios are marked `holdout: true`. They never appear in revision feedback, not even by ID. A contract passes only if the holdouts pass too; when only a holdout fails, the feedback says "a held-out scenario failed" and nothing more. This stops the authoring loop from fitting the visible scenarios.
178|
179|## 6. The investigation: loop, tools, actions and gates
180|
181|### 6.1 The loop
182|
183|Each turn, the gateway sends the full history to the Meta Model API (Responses API, `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, encrypted reasoning included and replayed; §8). The model returns one tool call; the platform runs it; the result, or the gate's refusal, goes back as the next input. The session is saved after every turn.
184|
185|- **One tool per turn.** A reply with no tool call gets "Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool." and counts as a turn. If a response holds more than one call, only the first runs.
186|- **Last turn.** On the final turn the SRE is told to submit with what it has.
187|- **Rationale.** Every tool call carries a required `rationale` (at most 200 characters). The model's reasoning tokens are not readable (Chat Completions returns no `reasoning_content`; Responses returns it encrypted), so `rationale` is the visible "think" line in the trace and the UI timeline.
188|- **Ending.**
189|
190|| Ends with | Incident goes to | Model calls afterwards |
191|| --- | --- | --- |
192|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `propose` | AWAITING_APPROVAL | None until approval or rejection |
193|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `none` | VERIFYING | None |
194|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `escalate` | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `escalated` | None until resumed |
195|| Three refused submissions | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `refused` | None until resumed |
196|| Turn limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `budget` | None until resumed |
197|| Token limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `token_budget` | None until resumed |
198|| The same read call a third time in a segment | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `stuck` | None until resumed |
199|| Model API still failing after retries | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `model_unavailable` | None until resumed |
200|
201|- **Resume.** A NEEDS_INPUT incident resumes the same session (hypotheses and evidence kept) only when a human replied, granted more turns, or the incident's tripwire state changed since it paused. Otherwise resume is refused without a model call. What changed is the SRE's next message.
202|- **Gates off (evals only).** Gates can be switched off to measure what they catch; each verdict they would have given is still recorded. The incident manager and the web app refuse an investigator with gates off.
203|
204|### 6.2 Read tools (proxied, read-only identity)
205|
206|Every read tool also takes `rationale`. Reads are capped per segment: 12 in the first, 4 more after each resume. A read over the cap is refused with an error, and the loop continues. A component that is not one of the service's component IDs is refused rather than answered with empty data.
207|
208|| Tool | Returns | Backed by |
209|| --- | --- | --- |
210|| `query_logs(deployment, window, filter)` | Log entries with `insertId` | `LogQuery` port |
211|| `get_resource(name)` | A connector instance, job instance, integration instance or environment | Mock Chronicle API `get` |
212|| `list_connector_logs(connectorInstance)` | Recent `ConnectorLog` records (empty unless log collection is on for that instance) | Mock `connectorInstances.logs.list` |
213|| `list_job_logs(jobInstance)` | Recent `JobInstanceLog` records | Mock `jobInstances.logs.list` |
214|| `test_integration_instance(name)` | Connectivity test result | Mock `integrationInstances.executeTest` (changes no state) |
215|| `compare_siblings(service, component, window)` | The same component's signals across every deployment of the service | Platform, computed |
216|| `tripwire_history(deployment)` | Recent trips, recoveries and approved changes | Platform state |
217|| `get_contract(service)` | Current contract and its last scorecard | Platform registry |
218|
219|### 6.3 Working tools and their gates
220|
221|The gates run inside these tools. A refused call returns `{"error": "...", "problems": ["..."]}` and never raises. Each problem starts with the rule it broke (`evidence.value: …`); the rule codes are listed in `docs/d5-pins.md`. Every tool result reaches the model as `{"callId": "...", "result": {...}}`, because the model cannot read call IDs back from the replayed history (D2 finding). A tool source's `field` is a dotted path into `result` (`successful`, not `result.successful`).
222|
223|| Tool | Does | Gate (inside the tool) |
224|| --- | --- | --- |
225|| `set_hypotheses(items)` | Sets 2–4 hypotheses, each with a statement and the evidence that would confirm it | 2–4 items; at least one marked `alternative: true` (a competing explanation, such as "this is fleet-wide, not specific to this tenant"). Required before `record_evidence` or `submit_diagnosis`. Calling it again replaces the set; evidence for removed hypotheses is dropped |
226|| `update_plan(plan)` | Records how the SRE will settle each hypothesis | None |
227|| `record_evidence(hypothesis, stance, source, why)` | Records one piece of evidence for (`supports`) or against (`refutes`) one hypothesis. `source` is `{insertId}` for a log entry or `{callId, field, value}` for a tool result | Log source: the `insertId` exists and belongs to the incident's deployment or to a sibling deployment the SRE queried in this session. Tool source: `callId` is a call made in this session and its result has `field` equal to `value`. The hypothesis exists. At most 3 items per hypothesis. Returns the evidence ID (`E1`, `E2`, …) and the hypotheses that still have no evidence |
228|| `submit_diagnosis(diagnosis)` | Submits the diagnosis (§6.5) | The submission rules in §6.5 |
229|
230|### 6.4 Action allowlist
231|
232|| Action | Notes |
233|| --- | --- |
234|| `connectorInstances.patch` | `updateMask` limited to `enabled`, `intervalSeconds`, `parameters` |
235|| `connectorInstances.restart` | Platform macro: patch `enabled=false`, then `enabled=true` |
236|| `connectorInstances.runOnDemand` | |
237|| `jobInstances.patch` | `updateMask` limited to `enabled`, `parameters` |
238|| `jobInstances.restart` | Platform macro: patch `enabled=false`, then `enabled=true` |
239|| `jobInstances.runOnDemand` | |
240|| `none` | No write: the fault has cleared (for example, after a human acted on an escalation). Goes straight to verification |
241|| `escalate` | Required when the fix is outside the allowlist (e.g. a credential rotation). Pauses the incident at NEEDS_INPUT |
242|
243|`connectorInstances.setLogsCollection` is not an action: turning on logging fixes nothing, so verification would fail it. The SRE can ask for it in an `escalationSummary`.
244|
245|### 6.5 Diagnosis schema and submission rules
246|
247|```json
248|{
249|  "incidentId": "string",
250|  "deployment": "string",
251|  "component": "string",
252|  "category": "connector_stalled | job_stalled | credential_failure | schema_drift | job_hollow_success | job_failing | unknown",
253|  "hypothesis": "ID of the hypothesis the SRE concludes (from set_hypotheses)",
254|  "summary": "the conclusion in one or two sentences",
255|  "evidence": ["E1", "E3"],
256|  "openQuestions": [ { "hypothesis": "string", "why": "string" } ],
257|  "action": {
258|    "type": "propose | none | escalate",
259|    "method": "one of the allowlist, when type is propose",
260|    "resource": "full resource name",
261|    "updateMask": ["field"],
262|    "patch": {},
263|    "escalationSummary": "string, when type is escalate"
264|  },
265|  "expectedVerification": { "tripwire": "string", "condition": "recovers_within", "seconds": 0 },
266|  "rollback": "string",
267|  "confidence": "low | medium | high"
268|}
269|```
270|
271|`category` is an enum so evaluations grade deterministically. The tool schema sets `additionalProperties: false` throughout.
272|
273|`submit_diagnosis` refuses a diagnosis, listing every problem, unless:
274|
275|1. **Schema.** It validates against the schema above.
276|2. **Recorded evidence only.** Every ID in `evidence` was recorded in this session.
277|3. **Hypothesis coverage.** The concluded hypothesis has at least one cited `supports` item. Every other hypothesis has at least one recorded `refutes` item or an entry in `openQuestions`.
278|4. **Category evidence rule.** The cited evidence includes what the category requires (table below).
279|5. **Action.** `propose`: the method is in §6.4, `updateMask` is within its allowed fields, the patch keys are within `updateMask`, and `resource` is the deployment's own connector instance (`connectorInstances.*`) or job instance (`jobInstances.*`). `propose` and `none`: `expectedVerification.tripwire` is a tripwire of the incident's deployment. `none`: at least one cited item was recorded after the session's most recent resume. `escalate`: `escalationSummary` is not empty.
280|
281|After three refused submissions the incident goes to NEEDS_INPUT with reason `refused`.
282|
283|**Category evidence rules.** These check deterministically that the evidence is the right kind for the conclusion. They stand in for the model-judged "claims check" other agents use.
284|
285|| Category | Cited evidence must include |
286|| --- | --- |
287|| `connector_stalled` | The deployment's latest `connector.run.completed` entry at or before the trip (that exact entry) |
288|| `job_stalled` | The deployment's latest `job.run.completed` entry at or before the trip (that exact entry) |
289|| `credential_failure` | A WARNING or ERROR entry from the deployment's connector, and a `test_integration_instance` result for the deployment's own integration instance with `successful: false` |
290|| `schema_drift` | An entry of the deployment that violates one of its schema tripwires |
291|| `job_hollow_success` | A `job.run.completed` entry of the deployment with `status: SUCCESS` and `indicatorsSynced: 0` |
292|| `job_failing` | A `job.run.error` entry, or a `job.run.completed` entry with `status: ERROR` |
293|| `unknown` | Nothing, but the action must be `escalate` |
294|
295|### 6.6 Guardrails
296|
297|- **Gates inside the tools** (§6.3, §6.5). Refusals are fed back to the model; nothing is retried silently.
298|- **Budgets.** Per segment of an investigation (the first run, then each resume): 24 turns, 12 read calls and 400,000 tokens (input plus output) at first, then `extra_turns` and 4 read calls per resume; all configurable. Two remediation attempts per incident.
299|- **Stuck detection.** The same read tool with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time in a segment pauses the session with reason `stuck` before the call runs. Working tools are exempt: repeating one changes state, and repeated refused submissions reach the refusal cap.
300|- **Concurrency.** The executor rejects a patch if the resource changed since the SRE read it.
301|- **Executor journal.** Append-only. Before any write the executor appends `intent` (approval ID, proposal hash, the resource version read at proposal time), then `started`, then `terminal` with the result. No write happens without a durable `intent` first. On restart, an `intent` without `terminal` is reconciled by re-reading the resource: if the change is already there it is marked done; otherwise it is applied once.
302|- **Recorded replay.** Live investigations chosen as fixtures (`fixtures/recorded/`) replay offline in CI through the scripted transport. Any difference in tool calls, gate verdicts or the final diagnosis blocks the merge.
303|- **Model calls.** Exponential backoff (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 s) on 429 and 5xx; a 120 s request timeout counts as a 5xx; diagnoses cached on the public instance; spend caps.
304|- **Import boundary.** `fleetsre.sre` may not import GCP clients or the Chronicle client directly; it reaches the world only through the tool set.

280|    manager = e2e["manager"]

296|) -> Any:
297|    """Step until the incident reaches `want` (or fail past the bound)."""
298|    manager = e2e["manager"]

88|            "environment": fault.environment,

90|        }

1|# D5 pins
2|
3|Interfaces and semantics of the D5 investigator as built (PRs #22–#27). `deliverables.md` §D5 and `spec.md` §6 summarise them; this file has the detail and wins where they differ. `tests/acceptance/d5/` encodes the testable rules; `tests/unit/` covers the rest.
4|
5|## Interfaces
6|
7|1. **`fleetsre/ports.py`.**
8|   - `LogQuery` protocol: `entries(start, end) -> list[LogEntry]`, `get(insert_id) -> LogEntry | None`; `MemoryLogQuery(sink)`.
9|   - `ChronicleClient` protocol: `get(name)`, `list_connector_logs(name, page_size)`, `list_job_logs(name, page_size)`, `execute_test(name)`, `patch(name, body, update_mask)`, `run_on_demand(name, body)`, `set_logs_collection(name, enabled)`, and an `identity` attribute. Returns parsed JSON or raises `ChronicleError(status, body)` carrying the Google error body.
10|   - `StateStore` protocol: `record_trip(event)`, `record_change(deployment, record)`, `trip_history(deployment) -> list[dict]`; `MemoryStateStore`.
11|2. **`fleetsre/adapters/chronicle_http.py`.** `ChronicleHttpClient(http: httpx.Client, identity: str)` sends `X-Fleetsre-Identity` (dev auth; ID tokens come in D7).
12|3. **`fleetsre/registry.py`.**
13|   - `Registry(contracts, deployments, scorecards=None)` with `contract(service)`, `deployments(service)`, `deployment(id)`, `scorecard(service)` and `route(entry) -> list[(deployment ID, component ID)]`, using the evaluator's routing (D4 semantics item 5). D6 adds `apply_contract`.
14|   - `Deployment.resource_names` maps component ID → full Chronicle resource name, plus `"integrationInstance"`. `deployments_from_fleet` computes it from the fleet; `Deployment.resources` keeps its D4 meaning (routing).
15|4. **Import boundary.** `fleetsre.sre` may import `fleetsre.registry`, `contracts`, `logmodel`, `ports`, `clock` and `evaluator.tripwires`. It must not reach `google`, `fleetsre.adapters` or `fleetsre.mock`, transitively included. `.importlinter` sets `exclude_type_checking_imports = True`.
16|5. **`ToolSet(log_query, chronicle, state, registry, *, clock, verification=True)`.**
17|   - `call(name, args, session, *, call_id=None)` always returns `{"callId": <id>, "result": <dict>}`: exactly what reaches the model.
18|   - A refusal's result is `{"error": str, "problems": [str]}`. `call` never raises; an internal error is a refusal with rule `tool.error`.
19|   - With `call_id=None` the ToolSet assigns `local-<n>`.
20|   - Every call is stored in `session.calls[call_id]` as a `CallRecord(tool, args, result, verdict, problems, turn)`.
21|   - The gates get the incident through `Incident.reconstruct(session.incident_id, registry, now)`, which parses the ID against the registry's services, environments and tripwire IDs (never by splitting on `-`).
22|   - Read-tool output schemas live in `fleetsre/sre/schemas.py` as `READ_TOOL_OUTPUT_SCHEMAS`.
23|6. **`Incident`** has `id`, `deployment`, `tripwire`, `opened_at`, `trip_event`, `service`, `component`, `resources` and `siblings`.
24|   - `resources` comes from `Deployment.resource_names`; `siblings` holds deployment IDs.
25|   - `Incident.from_trip(event, registry, now)` sets `id = f"inc-{service}-{environment}-{tripwire}-{at:%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ}"`.
26|   - `render_incident(incident, registry) -> str` builds the first user message: incident ID, deployment, `Component: <ID> (the tripped tripwire's component)`, every component of the service with its kind and full resource name, every tripwire with its component, the tripped tripwire's type and spec with `${param}` resolved (never the description text), trip reason, trip evidence insertIds, trippedAt, now, sibling IDs and budgets.
27|7. **`Evidence`** gains `deployment: str | None`. For a log source, `value` is `entry.model_dump(mode="json")`.
28|8. **`Session`** is JSON round-trippable.
29|   - Typed fields: `hypotheses: dict[str, Hypothesis]`, `evidence: dict[str, Evidence]`, `calls: dict[str, CallRecord]`.
30|   - Also: `turn`, `history` (input items), `segment_start_turn`, `turn_limit`, `read_limit`, `token_limit`, `segment_reads`, `segment_tokens`, `refused_submissions`, `resumed_at_turns`, `transcript_id` and `plan`.
31|   - `status` is `running | submitted | needs_input`.
32|   - `SessionStore`: `save`, `load`, `append_transcript(transcript_id, record)`, `transcript(transcript_id)`. Implementations: `MemorySessionStore()` (`fleetsre/sre/session.py`) and `SqliteSessionStore(path)` (`fleetsre/adapters/sqlite_state.py`).
33|9. **`investigate(incident, tools, gateway, store, *, max_turns=24, max_read_calls=12, max_tokens=400_000)`.**
34|   - With no saved session it starts one. With a saved `running` session it continues it with the budgets passed. With a saved `submitted` or `needs_input` session it raises `ValueError`.
35|   - `resume(incident, tools, gateway, store, *, message, extra_turns=8, extra_reads=4)` raises `ValueError` unless the saved session is `needs_input`.
36|   - Both return `InvestigationResult(diagnosis, status, reason, transcript_id, turns, read_calls, tokens, refusals)`. `status` is `submitted`, with `reason` the submitted action type (`propose` or `none`), or `needs_input` with a reason from pin 15. For `escalated`, `diagnosis` is set.
37|10. **`ModelGateway(config, transport, *, sleep=time.sleep)`.**
38|    - `ModelGateway.respond(role, input_items, tools)` returns `ModelResponse(output, usage)`; `tools` may be `None`.
39|    - `Transport.create(request: dict) -> dict` raises `TransportError(status)`.
40|    - `ScriptedTransport(responses)` records `.requests`; an item `{"_error": <status>}` raises `TransportError`.
41|    - `GatewayConfig.prices`: per model, USD per 1M tokens (`input`, `cached_input`, `output`).
42|    - `OpenAITransport(*, api_key, base_url)` calls the OpenAI SDK's `responses.create` with SDK `max_retries=0` and `timeout=120`. A timeout surfaces as `TransportError(504)`. The key is passed explicitly from `MODEL_API_KEY`.
43|    - The live role comes from `FLEETSRE_INVESTIGATE_MODEL` (default `muse-spark-1.3`), effort `medium`, prices from `FLEETSRE_PRICES_JSON`.
44|11. **Gate signatures.** `check_hypotheses(items)`; `check_evidence(args, session, log_query, incident, registry)`; `check_diagnosis(d, session, incident, contract, log_query, registry)`.
45|
46|## Loop
47|
48|12. **Input.** `[developer message: prompts/investigate.md verbatim, user message: render_incident] + history`.
49|    - Request flags: `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, `include=["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`, `reasoning={"effort": role effort}`, `tools=specs()`, `model` = role model.
50|    - Output items are replayed as returned (`exclude_none`).
51|13. **Tool outputs.** Every `function_call` gets a `function_call_output` whose `output` is the string `json.dumps({"callId", "result"})`. Only the first call in a response runs. The others get the error `not run: only the first tool call in a response runs`, and don't count as calls or toward stuck. A reply with no tool call gets the user message `Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool.` and counts as a turn.
52|14. **Last turn.** When `turn == turn_limit`, the user message `This is your last turn. Call submit_diagnosis now with what you have.` is appended before the request, after any plain-text message.
53|15. **Budgets are per segment.** The first investigation is segment 1, and each resume starts a new one.
54|    - Turns: `max_turns`, then `extra_turns`.
55|    - Reads: `max_read_calls`, then `extra_reads`. Only accepted calls to the eight read tools count. A read over the cap is refused (`reads.cap`) and still counts as a turn.
56|    - Tokens: `max_tokens`, counted from the segment start as usage input + output. The check runs after each turn; an accepted submission on that turn wins.
57|    - Three refused submissions in a segment end with `needs_input`/`refused`.
58|    - After a turn, the order is: accepted submission, then the refusal cap, then the token budget.
59|    - The refused-submission count and the stuck counts reset at each resume.
60|    - `needs_input` reasons: `escalated`, `refused`, `budget`, `token_budget`, `stuck`, `model_unavailable`.
61|16. **Stuck.** A read tool called with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time within a segment ends with `needs_input`/`stuck`, before the call runs. Only executed calls count (verdict `accepted` or `wouldRefuse`). Working tools never trip it: repeating one changes session state, and three identical refused submissions reach the refusal cap instead.
62|17. **Backoff.** 429 and 5xx retry with delays of 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 s (no jitter), up to `max_retries`, then `needs_input`/`model_unavailable`. Any other `TransportError` → `model_unavailable` at once. Other exceptions propagate.
63|18. **Transcript.** One record per turn, saved with the session after every turn. Each record holds the output items, the tool, args, verdict (`accepted | refused | wouldRefuse | no_tool_call | stuck`), problems, the output, usage (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`) and `cost_usd`.
64|
65|## Tools
66|
67|19. **`query_logs(deployment, window, filter, rationale)`.**
68|    - `window` is `{"lastMinutes": 1..360}`, relative to `clock.now()`.
69|    - `filter` is `{component?, event?, minSeverity?, runId?}`, `additionalProperties: false`. A `component` that is not a component ID of the deployment's contract is refused (`tool.name`), listing the valid IDs.

78|## Gates
79|
80|25. **Problem strings** take the form `<rule>: <text>`. Rules:
81|    - Order and hypotheses: `order`, `hypotheses.count`, `hypotheses.alternative`, `hypotheses.id`.
82|    - Evidence: `evidence.insert_id`, `evidence.deployment`, `evidence.future`, `evidence.call_id`, `evidence.field`, `evidence.value`, `evidence.hypothesis`, `evidence.limit`.
83|    - Diagnosis:
84|      - `diagnosis.schema`, with the JSON path of the problem (`diagnosis.schema: action: 'type' is a required property`). Argument-validation errors inside `diagnosis` use this rule, not `args.schema`.
85|      - `diagnosis.evidence`
86|      - `diagnosis.coverage`
87|      - `diagnosis.category` (includes `unknown` without `escalate`)
88|      - `diagnosis.action` (method outside the allowlist; empty `escalationSummary`)
89|      - `diagnosis.update_mask` (mask outside the method's fields, or patch keys outside the mask)
90|      - `diagnosis.resource`
91|      - `diagnosis.incident` (`incidentId` or `deployment`)
92|      - `diagnosis.component`, listing the contract's component IDs
93|      - `diagnosis.hypothesis`
94|      - `diagnosis.verification` (missing, or a tripwire not of this deployment)
95|      - `diagnosis.none_after_resume`
96|    - Other: `reads.cap`, `tool.unknown`, `tool.name`, `tool.error`, `args.schema` (with the JSON path).
97|26. **`set_hypotheses`.** Items are `{id, statement, wouldConfirm, alternative}`, all four required. IDs match `^H[1-9][0-9]*$` and are unique. 2–4 items, at least one alternative. Replacing the set keeps evidence whose hypothesis ID remains.
98|27. **`record_evidence`.**
99|    - **Log source:** the insertId exists, its timestamp is ≤ now, and it routes (via `Registry.route`) to the incident's deployment or to a sibling queried in this session (via `query_logs` on it, or `compare_siblings`). There is no other fallback.
100|    - **Tool source:** `callId` is an accepted read-tool call of this session. `field` is a dotted path into the result, where numeric segments index lists and a leading `result.` is stripped. `value` must match by JSON equality, with no coercion.
101|    - At most 3 items per hypothesis. IDs are `E<n>`, and `recordedAtTurn` is the session turn.
102|28. **`submit_diagnosis`** checks, in addition to spec §6.5:
103|    - The schema first. A schema problem always refuses, gates on or off. With gates on and no hypotheses yet, the order problem is reported first.
104|    - `incidentId` and `deployment` equal the incident's.
105|    - `component` is a component ID of the deployment's contract.
106|    - `hypothesis` is a current hypothesis.
107|    - For `propose`: a `connectorInstances.*` method needs the deployment's connector instance name, and a `jobInstances.*` method its job instance name, by exact match. The integration instance is never a valid resource. The patch keys are within `updateMask`.
108|    - `expectedVerification` is required for `propose` and `none`, and optional for `escalate`.
109|    - For `none`: an item counts as recorded after the last resume iff `recordedAtTurn > max(resumed_at_turns)`. With no resume, every item counts.
110|    - Repeated submissions to the ToolSet are allowed; the loop ends at the first accepted one.
111|29. **Category rules** (the spec §6.5 table, tightened):
112|    - `connector_stalled` / `job_stalled`: the cited log evidence includes, by insertId, the deployment's latest heartbeat at or before `trip_event.at`. The heartbeat is the event of the cadence tripwire on the contract's `connectorInstance` (`jobInstance`) component, whatever the incident's component, so a canary incident can be diagnosed `connector_stalled`.
113|    - `credential_failure`: an entry from the deployment's connector at or above WARNING, plus a `test_integration_instance` call on the deployment's own integration instance with `successful: false`.
114|    - `schema_drift`: an entry that routes to the incident's deployment and for which `evaluator.tripwires.schema_violation` returns a reason. `schema_violation` applies the tripwire's `event`/`where` filters itself; `${param}` is resolved.
115|    - `job_hollow_success`: a `job.run.completed` of the deployment with `status: SUCCESS` and `indicatorsSynced: 0`.
116|    - `job_failing`: a `job.run.error` entry, or a `job.run.completed` with `status: ERROR`, of the deployment.
117|30. **`verification=False`.** The order, hypotheses, evidence and diagnosis rules 2–5 record `wouldRefuse`, with their problems, instead of refusing. Schema problems (`args.schema`, `diagnosis.schema`) still refuse. Budgets, the read cap and stuck still apply.
118|31. **The right component** for evaluation is the tripped tripwire's component.
119|
120|## Recording and evaluation
121|
122|32. **`make record FAULT=<F>`** runs one live investigation on the scripted fixture's world and writes `fixtures/recorded/<F>.json`, containing `{fault, seed, t0, faults, incident, responses, transcript, diagnosis}`. Every `encrypted_content` value is replaced with `"<stripped>"` at record time. Committed recordings: F1, F2, F3 (#26).
123|33. **Live eval (T19/T20)** writes `evals/d5-<UTC date>.json`: per run the status, reason, turns, reads, tokens, cost, refusals by rule, tools called and diagnosis; plus the F2 probe share and, per fault, one gates-off run's outcome with its would-refuse and refused counts by rule.

2|
3|from dataclasses import dataclass, field
4|from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
5|from pathlib import Path
6|
7|from fleetsre.clock import SimClock
8|from fleetsre.contracts import Contract
9|from fleetsre.evaluator.canary import CanaryScheduler
10|from fleetsre.evaluator.engine import Evaluator, TripEvent
11|from fleetsre.harness.scenario import Expected, Scenario
12|from fleetsre.mock.fleet import load_fleet
13|from fleetsre.mock.world import World
14|from fleetsre.ports import MemorySink
15|from fleetsre.registry import deployments_from_fleet
16|
17|T0 = datetime(2026, 10, 29, 14, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
18|
19|
20|@dataclass
21|class ScenarioResult:
22|    """Result of replaying one scenario.
23|
24|    latencies maps (kind, deployment_id, tripwire) to seconds, where kind is
25|    "trip" or "recovery" and deployment_id is "<service>/<environment>".
26|    missing holds (kind, deployment_id, tripwire) for expected items with no
27|    actual match within withinSeconds. unexpected holds actual events matched
28|    by no expected item (mustNotTrip violations included).
29|    """
30|
31|    scenario_id: str
32|    expected: Expected
33|    actual: list[TripEvent] = field(default_factory=list)
34|    latencies: dict[tuple[str, str, str], float] = field(default_factory=dict)
35|    missing: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
36|    unexpected: list[TripEvent] = field(default_factory=list)
37|    passed: bool = False
38|
39|
40|def _fleet_path() -> Path:
41|    return (
42|        Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
43|        / "fixtures"
44|        / "fleet.yaml"
45|    )
46|
47|
48|def _latest_fault_at(
49|    scenario: Scenario, environment: str, at: datetime
50|) -> datetime | None:
51|    best: datetime | None = None
52|    for fault in scenario.faults:
53|        ref = T0 + timedelta(seconds=fault.at)
54|        if fault.environment == environment and ref <= at:
55|            if best is None or ref > best:
56|                best = ref
57|    return best
58|
59|
60|def _latest_clear_at(
61|    scenario: Scenario, environment: str, at: datetime
62|) -> datetime | None:
63|    best: datetime | None = None
64|    for fault in scenario.faults:
65|        if fault.environment != environment or fault.clearAt is None:
66|            continue
67|        ref = T0 + timedelta(seconds=fault.clearAt)
68|        if ref <= at and (best is None or ref > best):
69|            best = ref
70|    if best is not None:
71|        return best
72|    return _latest_fault_at(scenario, environment, at)
73|
74|
75|def run_scenario(
76|    contract: Contract, scenario: Scenario, *, tick_seconds: int = 15
77|) -> ScenarioResult:
78|    """Replay one scenario against its contract on a SimClock."""
79|    fleet = load_fleet(_fleet_path())
80|    clock = SimClock(T0)
81|    sink = MemorySink()
82|    world = World(fleet, scenario.seed, clock, sink)
83|    items: list[dict[str, object]] = []
84|    for fault in scenario.faults:
85|        item: dict[str, object] = {
86|            "at": fault.at,
87|            "type": fault.type,
88|            "environment": fault.environment,
89|            "params": dict(fault.params),
90|        }
91|        target = getattr(fault, "target", None)
92|        if target is not None:
93|            item["target"] = target
94|        if fault.clearAt is not None:
95|            item["clearAt"] = fault.clearAt
96|        items.append(item)
97|    world.schedule(items)
98|    deployments = deployments_from_fleet(fleet, contract, scenario.deployments)
99|    evaluator = Evaluator([contract], deployments, clock)
100|    scheduler = CanaryScheduler(world, evaluator, [contract], clock)
101|    actual: list[TripEvent] = []
102|    consumed = 0
103|    steps = scenario.durationSeconds // tick_seconds
104|    for step in range(steps + 1):
105|        tick_at = T0 + timedelta(seconds=step * tick_seconds)
106|        clock.set(tick_at)
107|        scheduler.tick()
108|        world.step_until(tick_at)
109|        entries = sink.entries
110|        while consumed < len(entries):
111|            actual.extend(evaluator.ingest(entries[consumed]))
112|            consumed += 1
113|        actual.extend(evaluator.tick())
114|
115|    latencies: dict[tuple[str, str, str], float] = {}
116|    missing: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
117|    unexpected: list[TripEvent] = []
118|    matched = [False] * len(actual)
119|    by_key: dict[tuple[str, str, str], list[int]] = {}
120|    for index, event in enumerate(actual):
121|        by_key.setdefault(
122|            (event.kind, event.deployment, event.tripwire), []
123|        ).append(index)
124|    for trip in scenario.expected.trips:
125|        dep_id = f"{scenario.service}/{trip.deployment}"
126|        key = ("trip", dep_id, trip.tripwire)
127|        hit = False
128|        for index in by_key.get(key, []):
129|            if matched[index]:
130|                continue
131|            ref = _latest_fault_at(
132|                scenario, trip.deployment, actual[index].at
133|            )
134|            if ref is None:
135|                continue
136|            latency = (actual[index].at - ref).total_seconds()
137|            if 0 <= latency <= trip.withinSeconds:
138|                matched[index] = True
139|                latencies[key] = latency
140|                hit = True
141|                break
142|        if not hit:
143|            missing.append(key)
144|    for recovery in scenario.expected.recoveries:
145|        dep_id = f"{scenario.service}/{recovery.deployment}"
146|        key = ("recovery", dep_id, recovery.tripwire)
147|        hit = False
148|        for index in by_key.get(key, []):
149|            if matched[index]:
150|                continue
151|            ref = _latest_clear_at(
152|                scenario, recovery.deployment, actual[index].at
153|            )
154|            if ref is None:
155|                continue
156|            latency = (actual[index].at - ref).total_seconds()
157|            if 0 <= latency <= recovery.withinSeconds:
158|                matched[index] = True
159|                latencies[key] = latency
160|                hit = True
161|                break
162|        if not hit:
163|            missing.append(key)
164|    for index, event in enumerate(actual):
165|        if not matched[index]:
166|            unexpected.append(event)
167|    return ScenarioResult(
168|        scenario_id=scenario.id,
169|        expected=scenario.expected,
170|        actual=actual,
171|        latencies=latencies,
172|        missing=missing,
173|        unexpected=unexpected,
174|        passed=(not missing and not unexpected),
175|    )

1|# D5 pins
2|
3|Interfaces and semantics of the D5 investigator as built (PRs #22–#27). `deliverables.md` §D5 and `spec.md` §6 summarise them; this file has the detail and wins where they differ. `tests/acceptance/d5/` encodes the testable rules; `tests/unit/` covers the rest.
4|
5|## Interfaces
6|
7|1. **`fleetsre/ports.py`.**
8|   - `LogQuery` protocol: `entries(start, end) -> list[LogEntry]`, `get(insert_id) -> LogEntry | None`; `MemoryLogQuery(sink)`.
9|   - `ChronicleClient` protocol: `get(name)`, `list_connector_logs(name, page_size)`, `list_job_logs(name, page_size)`, `execute_test(name)`, `patch(name, body, update_mask)`, `run_on_demand(name, body)`, `set_logs_collection(name, enabled)`, and an `identity` attribute. Returns parsed JSON or raises `ChronicleError(status, body)` carrying the Google error body.
10|   - `StateStore` protocol: `record_trip(event)`, `record_change(deployment, record)`, `trip_history(deployment) -> list[dict]`; `MemoryStateStore`.
11|2. **`fleetsre/adapters/chronicle_http.py`.** `ChronicleHttpClient(http: httpx.Client, identity: str)` sends `X-Fleetsre-Identity` (dev auth; ID tokens come in D7).
12|3. **`fleetsre/registry.py`.**
13|   - `Registry(contracts, deployments, scorecards=None)` with `contract(service)`, `deployments(service)`, `deployment(id)`, `scorecard(service)` and `route(entry) -> list[(deployment ID, component ID)]`, using the evaluator's routing (D4 semantics item 5). D6 adds `apply_contract`.
14|   - `Deployment.resource_names` maps component ID → full Chronicle resource name, plus `"integrationInstance"`. `deployments_from_fleet` computes it from the fleet; `Deployment.resources` keeps its D4 meaning (routing).
15|4. **Import boundary.** `fleetsre.sre` may import `fleetsre.registry`, `contracts`, `logmodel`, `ports`, `clock` and `evaluator.tripwires`. It must not reach `google`, `fleetsre.adapters` or `fleetsre.mock`, transitively included. `.importlinter` sets `exclude_type_checking_imports = True`.
